news.126: Option to draw offcut cuts (simple or detailed), and options grouped under “Method”. Origin in the centre or mid-edge: more compact group of parts.
news.125: Faster free rotation, no extra panel depending on the chosen origin, smaller origin marker that is always fully visible.
news.124: Fix: parts could overlap with the origin in the centre. Grouping around the origin never needs more panels.
news.123: Option to export the panel outline with the parts (on its own layer). Parts are grouped in a compact block around the chosen origin.
dl.board: Include the panel outline in exports
news.122: Safer SVG import: only the file’s geometry is kept. Automated tests and reorganised code.

news.111: List of what’s new in the settings.
news.110: Part names and layers, sorting, LightBurn, VectorCraft, HPGL and SVGZ import, per-part scale and duplication.
news.109: New logo: the N straight on the blue background.
news.108: Free rotation in 5° steps, rotation setting for all parts, SVG import fixed.
news.107: The page loads from the network when online, so icons stay up to date.
news.106: Icons renamed to force an update on devices.
news.105: New logo, drawn Nestor title, blueprint-style background and translated title block.
news.112: Full version history and a button to report a bug on GitHub.
news.100: First version: nesting DXF, SVG and AI parts on sheets, SVG and DXF export, installable app in 45 languages.
bug.title: A problem?
bug.hint: Opens a report on GitHub, already filled in with technical details (GitHub account needed, the report is public). Your file is never sent: attach it yourself if you want.
news.113: New PolyForm Perimeter license: free use for everyone, including at work, but no resale or competing copies. Name and logo reserved.
origin.title: Origin (machine zero)
origin.hint: Parts are grouped from this point, and it is the zero of the exported files.
news.120: Portrait sheets, import of several files and adding to the current job, choice of the origin (machine zero).
calc.many: {n} parts to place: this may take a while.
news.121: Quantities are no longer capped at 500, oversized parts are reported right away, and a Cancel button appears during a long calculation.
news.140: New Milling tab: spindle speed, feed rate and depth of cut for your cutter, material and machine.
news.130: Lighter app (only one language loaded) and better protected (page security policy, oversized SVGZ files rejected). Clear message for a damaged PDF. Code reorganised and better tested. Fix: right after an update, the app could keep part of the old version (offcut cuts had no effect on iPhone). PDF/AI reader updated (pdf.js 6.5).

mill.title: Milling settings
mill.famEx.medium: oak, beech, birch plywood, hard plastics
mill.rule: Chip load {c} mm per flute (Ø / {k}), depth {f} × Ø.
mill.prudent: Cautious starting values: listen to the machine and adjust. On a less rigid machine or without dust extraction, reduce the depth.
mill.invalid: Enter the cutter diameter and number of flutes.
mill.noteMax: Your spindle tops out at {n} rpm: the feed is reduced to keep the same chip load.
mill.noteMin: Your spindle cannot go below {n} rpm: the feed is increased to keep the same chip load.
mill.noteFeedMax: Your machine cannot feed faster than {n} mm/min: the spindle speed is lowered to keep the same chip load.
mill.noteThinChip: Even at your spindle’s lowest speed, you would need to feed faster than {n} mm/min: the chip will be thinner than advised and the cutter may heat up. A cutter with fewer flutes helps.
mill.noteMelt: Plastic that melts: prefer a single-flute cutter, which makes a bigger chip.
mill.noteDowncut: Downcut spiral: chips stay in the groove. If it heats up, reduce the depth.
mill.noteCompression: Compression: the first pass must be deeper than the upcut part of the cutter.
